title: Louis CK created the masterpiece TV show Louie. Why do his movies fall short?

commenti.body:
Good art takes collaboration. Yes, he has all those credits on his show, but there were still a dozen other creatives helping him achieve this vision.

He also seems like someone who manipulates and uses the people around him. The longer one does that, the less, actually talented people, will stay around them, because they have options.

It's likely Louie was just a perfect storm, and he otherwise does not have the ability to reach those heights/drove away those who helped him there.
Eh he has Horace and Pete too which I thought was pretty remarkable.

Because TV isn't film.

And he's one of many comedians who have no business thinking of themselves as directors (Gervais, Rock, Seinfeld, Burr).

The only successful one of that batch was Peele, who genuinely understands the cinematic form, had eclectic interests and was willing to push himself beyond the comedy genre.

On the other end of the spectrum, Richard Curtis is no one's idea of a great director but spent years writing scripts for other people to direct and learned a lot about filmmaking before he made his directorial debut.

So you don't necessarily need to be a very good director like Peele but you need to understand the way in which a proper director crafts a film.

That CK spent his screenwriting career butchering "Heaven Can Wait" and "Chloe in the Afternoon" for other idiots like Chris Rock showed he had no business becoming a director himself.
Chris Rock is plenty of things but I wouldn't go as far as to call him an idiot.

He's a terrible director.

So bad that he doesn't even know he's bad and doesn't even attempt to improve.

He also seems like someone who manipulates and uses the people around him. 

That's interesting speculation. How do you know this?
Observations of his character, and the reports of people who have worked with him.
